pairs.title: Attention is all you need
pairs.claim: The Transformer relies entirely on attention mechanisms and dispenses with recurrence and convolutions.
pairs.excerpt: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

pairs.title: BERT: Pre-training of deep bidirectional transformers for language understanding
pairs.claim: BERT pre-trains deep bidirectional representations by jointly conditioning on left and right context.
pairs.excerpt: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.

pairs.title: Retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks
pairs.claim: Retrieval-augmented generation combines a pre-trained parametric memory with a non-parametric memory of retrieved text.
pairs.excerpt: We explore a general-purpose fine-tuning recipe for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) — models which combine pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory for language generation. Our RAG models generate more specific, diverse and factual language than a state-of-the-art parametric-only seq2seq baseline.

pairs.title: Adam: A method for stochastic optimization
pairs.claim: Adam is a first-order gradient-based method for optimizing stochastic objective functions.
pairs.excerpt: We introduce Adam, an algorithm for first-order gradient-based optimization of stochastic objective functions, based on adaptive estimates of lower-order moments. The method is straightforward to implement, is computationally efficient, has little memory requirements, and is well suited for problems that are large in terms of data and/or parameters.

pairs.title: Retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks
pairs.claim: RAG achieves state-of-the-art results on three open-domain QA tasks and eliminates hallucination entirely.
pairs.excerpt: For parametric seq2seq models, RAG achieves state-of-the-art results on three open-domain QA tasks, outperforming parametric seq2seq models and task-specific retrieve-and-extract architectures. Our RAG models generate more specific, diverse and factual language than a state-of-the-art parametric-only seq2seq baseline.

pairs.title: Language models are few-shot learners
pairs.claim: GPT-3 achieves strong few-shot performance across many benchmarks and can run on consumer hardware.
pairs.excerpt: We train GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, and test its performance in the few-shot setting. GPT-3 achieves strong performance on many NLP datasets, including translation, question-answering, and cloze tasks, without any gradient updates or fine-tuning.

pairs.title: Deep residual learning for image recognition
pairs.claim: Residual networks cannot be trained beyond 20 layers without performance degradation.
pairs.excerpt: We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions. We provide comprehensive empirical evidence showing that these residual networks are easier to optimize, and can gain accuracy from considerably increased depth. On the ImageNet dataset we evaluate residual nets with a depth of up to 152 layers—8× deeper than VGG nets but still having lower complexity.

pairs.title: BERT: Pre-training of deep bidirectional transformers for language understanding
pairs.claim: BERT is a unidirectional left-to-right language model.
pairs.excerpt: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Unlike recent language representation models, BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.

pairs.title: Adam: A method for stochastic optimization
pairs.claim: Attention mechanisms improve machine translation quality.
pairs.excerpt: We introduce Adam, an algorithm for first-order gradient-based optimization of stochastic objective functions, based on adaptive estimates of lower-order moments. The method is straightforward to implement, is computationally efficient, has little memory requirements, and is invariant to diagonal rescaling of the gradients.

pairs.title: Deep residual learning for image recognition
pairs.claim: Retrieval-augmented generation improves factual accuracy of language models.
pairs.excerpt: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We evaluate residual nets on the ImageNet dataset and show strong results on object detection benchmarks.

unsup_bert_dir.rationale: 原文片段明确指出BERT是双向（bidirectional）模型，同时利用左右上下文，这与论断中声称的“单向从左到右”直接矛盾。

irr_adam_vs_attention.label: undetermined

irr_adam_vs_attention.rationale: 原文片段仅介绍了Adam优化算法的特性，未提及注意力机制（Attention mechanisms）或机器翻译（machine translation），因此无法判断其是否支持该论断。

irr_resnet_vs_rag.label: undetermined
irr_resnet_vs_rag.evidence: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously.
irr_resnet_vs_rag.rationale: 被引文献片段讨论的是计算机视觉中的深度残差网络训练问题，与论断中关于检索增强生成（RAG）提升语言模型事实准确性的内容完全无关。
